text: First video is finally out. I went to meet Yerzhan Ryskali, founder of Clockster, to understand how startup funding actually works in Central Asia. One of the most interesting things I've noticed since moving here is how different the venture capital ecosystem is compared to the US or UK. There isn't anywhere near the same depth of private capital, so governments, state-backed funds and government-incentivized banks have ended up playing a much bigger role. We talked about how this works in Uzbekistan, why Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have developed differently, what it's actually like raising money here, and some of the problems Central Asian startups face once they reach the point where they need serious capital to expand. This is the first proper video from the media company I've been building here. Still a lot to improve, but we're going to keep putting these out and documenting the region as it develops. Would appreciate any feedback, especially criticism.

Front-end implied volatility remains near the lower end of its recent range and downside skew has moderated, even as the macro backdrop stays mixed. US manufacturing strengthened in July, but labour indicators have softened. JOLTS openings fell to 7.36m and ADP payrolls rose by only 44k, putting today's US employment report firmly in focus. With domestic yields rising and the BOJ still holding around half of outstanding JGBs, Japanese funding conditions remain relevant well beyond the FX market.
